The '''Juventus FC–AC Milan rivalry''' is the oldest running [[Football in Italy|italian football]] [[List of sports rivalries|rivalry]] and one of its most played matches, having taken place for the first time in an official game in 1901. Both [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] and [[AC Milan|Milan]] rank among the most successful clubs in [[Italy]], the first for being the most successful team domestically and the latter on the international stage. From a historical point of view, they are both held to similar standards, consequently making them direct competitors to reach the same goals or honours more often than not.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.acmilan.com/it/news/show/144517 |title=Milan-Juve in Field History |publisher=AC Milan |access-date=22 November 2012}}</ref>

=== Records ===
*'''Largest victory''': Milan 8–1 Juventus ([[1911–12 Italian Football Championship|1911–12]])
*'''Most goals in a game''': Juventus 8–2 Milan ([[1926–27 Divisione Nazionale|1926–27]])
*'''Biggest win for Juventus''': Juventus 8–2 Milan ([[1926–27 Divisione Nazionale|1926–27]]); Juventus 6–0 Milan ([[1925–26 Prima Divisione|1925–26]]) 
*'''Biggest win for Milan''': Milan 8–1 Juventus ([[1911–12 Italian Football Championship|1911–12]])
*'''Highest scoring draw''': Juventus 3–3 Milan ([[1930–31 Serie A|1930–31]]); Milan 3–3 Juventus ([[1946–47 Serie A|1946–47]])
*'''Biggest away win for Juventus''': Milan 1–6 Juventus ([[1996–97 Serie A|1996–97]])
*'''Biggest away win for Milan''': Juventus 1–7 Milan ([[1949–50 Serie A|1949–50]])

</div>
• '''Total:''' Milan with '''34''' higher finishes, Juventus with '''56''' higher finishes, and '''1''' equal finish (as of the end of the 2025–26 season). No head-to-heads in [[1980–81 Serie A|1981]] and [[1982–83 Serie A|1983]], since Milan was in [[Serie B]], and in [[2006–07 Serie A|2007]], since Juventus was in [[Serie B]].

'''Notes''':
* [[1945–46 Italian Football Championship]] is not included in [[Football records and statistics in Italy|Serie A statistics]].
* Both teams finished with the same number of points in [[1947–48 Serie A|1948]], and the regulation of the time did not contemplate tiebreakers: both teams finished in second place.
* Both teams finished with the same number of points in [[1984–85 Serie A|1985]], and Milan finished ahead, on head-to-head points.
* Both teams finished with the same number of points in [[2008–09 Serie A|2009]], and Juventus finished ahead, on head-to-head points.
* Due to the [[Calciopoli]] scandal, Juventus' [[2004–05 Serie A|2004–05 title]] was voided, while in the [[2005–06 Serie A|2005–06 season]] Juventus was relegated and the title was awarded to [[Inter Milan]] as AC Milan suffered a 30-point deduction from its initial 2nd-place finish.
